newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen firming at open.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen firming at open.

text.p: U.S. stocks were expected to rise at the market open on Wednesday, extending gains after Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on the economy yesterday, which allayed fears of an imminent interest rate increase.

"I think the market should open with a better tone," Gail Dudack, chief investment strategist at UBS Securities, said. The Standard & Poor's 500 futures index rose 2.30 points to 944.55 and the long bond dipped 1/32 to 6.42 percent.
Analysts said the market would draw strength from Greenspan's upbeat report and solid earnings results.
